page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is a compute-oriented virtual server deployed on KVM hypervisors. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, offering 2 shared vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core. Memory allocation stands at 2.0 GB (1.0 GB per vCPU), backed by 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 64 KB of L1 data cache. Modern instruction extensions are broadly supported, including AVX-512 variants (F, VNNI, BF16), AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and AES cryptography flags. No dedicated GPU hardware is included. Storage is bundled directly with a 50 GB local SSD, and networking includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-threaded compute efficiency. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance scored 3787.27, positioning it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. High single-thread throughput is further evidenced by compression results, achieving 40.69 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 17.42 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, both ranking in the top tier. Conversely, multi-core metrics settle into average or weak bands due to the two-core shared configuration, recording a stress-ng multi-core score of 7763.62 and a PassMark CPU score of 6709.35.

System memory and data operations show clear constraints related to capacity and density. The PassMark memory test registered 950.54, falling into the bottom 10 percent, while uncached memory bandwidth sustains 63.77 GB/sec for large reads and 45.7 GB/sec for large writes. Database benchmarks mirror this lower tier, with PassMark database operations at 2404.76, though Redis SET operations remain competitive at 6.18 million operations per second and static web throughput reaches 10.31 GB/sec. Small language model inference (135M parameters) delivers 712.08 prompt tokens per second and 186.2 generation tokens per second.

Considering its low RAM-to-vCPU ratio and shared CPU model, the PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB provides cost-effective access to modern Zen 5 architecture without paying for dedicated cores or high memory footprints. It is best suited for lightweight web serving, microservices, small API gateways, single-threaded processing utilities, and routine CI/CD build scripts where heavy parallel scaling and large in-memory caches are not required.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-2GB is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on KVM virtualization and powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 shared vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 2.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 50 GB local SSD, alongside 1 public IPv4 address. The server incorporates modern instruction sets, including AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES-NI, but does not feature a dedicated GPU. Performance data highlights top-tier single-threaded capability, demonstrated by top 10 percent finishes in single-core stress-ng tests and gzip compression. However, limited RAM capacity and shared CPU topology constrain multi-core throughput and memory-intensive operations, as shown by lower PassMark memory and database results. This profile makes the instance cost-efficient and practical for lightweight web serving, background processing jobs, microservices, and general low-memory compute utilities.
